title: Karlovac Cost Guide 2027: Prices for Stay, Food, Sights
metaDescription: Karlovac prices for 2027: hotels from about €60, meals from €10, beer around €2.20, Aquatika €12, Dubovac Castle €3. Budgets and money-saving tips.
content:
## How Much Does a Day in Karlovac Cost?

Karlovac sits about 55 km from Zagreb and costs noticeably less than the capital. A cheap meal is about €10 here against about €12 in Zagreb, and a mid-range dinner for two is about €40 against about €60. A draft beer is around €2.20 against €3.00.

### Daily budget estimates

| Style | Per person per day | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Budget | €50–70 | Private room or apartment share, supermarket and bakery food, one inexpensive restaurant meal, one sight |
| Mid-range | €110–160 | 4-star hotel (half of a double room), two restaurant meals, coffees, beers, attractions |
| Comfortable | €180+ | Best hotel, a three-course dinner with wine, a guided tour, taxis |

These are estimates built from typical hotel rates and restaurant prices. Final costs depend heavily on the season and on how many people share a room.

## Accommodation Prices in Karlovac

Karlovac has roughly 46 hotels listed on Tripadvisor and more than 160 places to stay on Booking, including many apartments and guesthouses. Most are not on the coast-style tourist price scale. Rates for a double room usually start around €50–60 for simple private rooms and apartments.

### Hotels

- **Aminess Kadoor Hotel:** four-star, roughly €90–100 per night for two. It has the strongest value ratings among the main hotels.
- **Boutique Hotel Korana Srakovčić:** about €110–115 per night. It has a pool and a spa, and is popular with guests who want a quiet riverside stay.
- **Aminess Florian & Godler Hotel:** about €115–120 per night. It has a pool and the highest guest score of the main hotels.
- **Hotel Europa:** four-star, mid-priced, with a fitness area and a spa.

Seasonal swings are modest compared with the coast. Winter (December–February) averages are the lowest, and the average nightly price in the warmer months is roughly 15–25% higher. Karlovac is mostly a stop-over town, so weekday prices can be cheaper than weekends when events are on.

### Apartments and rooms

Apartments with self check-in are common and usually cost less than the hotels. They are a good choice for stays of two nights or more, because a kitchen cuts food costs. Free parking is common at apartments, whereas some hotels charge for it, so check before booking.

## Food and Drink Prices

### Restaurants

- Inexpensive restaurant meal: about €10 (range €10–17)
- Three-course dinner for two at a mid-range restaurant, without drinks: about €40
- Mid-range bottle of wine in a restaurant: about €6
- Fast-food combo: roughly €7–8

Karlovac is known across Croatia for river fish, lamb and its Karlovačko beer brewery tradition. Fish dishes from the Korana, Kupa and Mrežnica region are usually priced above standard grilled meat, so expect €14–22 for a main course at a sit-down restaurant.

### Coffee and beer

- Cappuccino: about €1.80 (range €1.60–3.00)
- Domestic draft beer, 0.5 L: about €2.20 (up to about €6 in tourist-oriented venues)
- Bottled water: about €1.50
- Soft drink: about €2.10
- Supermarket local beer (0.5 L can): about €1.50–1.80

Karlovačko is the local beer. Karlovac prices for it are among the lowest in Croatia, which makes a riverside drink one of the best-value activities in town.

### Self-catering

Supermarkets, bakeries and the daily market keep a picnic lunch to about €5–8 per person. A burek or sandwich from a bakery is the cheapest hot food in town.

## Attraction and Activity Prices

### Aquatika Freshwater Aquarium

Aquatika, on Branka Čavlovića Čavleka 1a, shows the fish of the Kupa, Korana, Mrežnica and Dobra rivers. Adults pay €12, children 3–14 pay €7, and students, pensioners and teenagers 15–18 pay €8. A family ticket (2 adults and 3 children) costs €24, and each extra child is €3. Annual passes cost €35 for adults and €25 for children. Audio guides are about €2.50. It opens daily 9:00–19:00 from 1 April to 31 October and 9:00–17:00 from 1 November to 31 March. It is closed on Easter, Christmas and New Year.

Most visitors need 30–60 minutes. For adults travelling alone, €12 is on the high side for the time involved, and some reviewers call it pricey. Families get better value from the family ticket.

### Dubovac Castle

The old town of Dubovac sits on a hill above the Kupa and Korana confluence. Adult tickets cost €3, children, students and retirees €2, and a family ticket €5. Guided tours cost €10 in Croatian and €20 in English. The museum is typically open Tuesday to Sunday and closed on Mondays, so check hours before the uphill walk.

The views from the surrounding hill and courtyard cost nothing. The tower view is the main reason to pay the ticket.

### Free things to do

- Walking Zrinjevac park and the old fortress ramparts
- Riverside paths along the Korana and Kupa
- The old town square and the Dubovac hill walk
- Summer swimming spots on the Korana river (free, no facilities)

## Transport Costs

Karlovac is about 55 km from Zagreb and roughly 1 hour away by train or bus. Public transport from Zagreb is far cheaper than any private transfer; a private door-to-door tour from Zagreb is listed at about €560 per group of up to 3, which is not worth it for most travelers. The centre is compact and walkable, so taxis are rarely needed. Parking near Aquatika is free, which suits drivers.

## Money-Saving Tips for Karlovac

- **Skip the guided castle tour.** The English-language tour costs €20, which is nearly seven times the entry fee. Pay the €3 ticket and read the displays instead.
- **Stay out of the hotels on the busiest weekends.** Apartments on weekdays are the cheapest option.
- **Eat lunch as the main meal.** Many restaurants offer a set daily menu at lunch that costs less than the same dishes at dinner.
- **Buy beer in a local café, not a hotel bar.** The difference can be €1–3 per pint.
- **Look into the Karlovac Cultural Card.** It reduces Dubovac Castle tickets to €1 and the English tour to €5.
- **Combine Karlovac with a day trip.** Karlovac is cheaper than Zagreb for overnight stays, so some visitors sleep here and day-trip to the capital.

## Is Karlovac Cheap Compared With Other Croatian Cities?

Yes. Prices run below Zagreb and well below Dalmatian coast towns in summer. Restaurants and drinks are the biggest difference. The savings are the largest on accommodation in July and August, when coastal rates peak but Karlovac stays steady.

## Opinion: Where to Spend and Where to Save

Spend your money on a riverside dinner and a Korana-side hotel, not on the aquarium. Aquatika is pleasant but short, and the €12 adult ticket is the least efficient spend in town. The free river walk to Dubovac and a €3 tower ticket give better value.

faq.question: How much money do I need per day in Karlovac?
faq.answer: Budget travelers can manage on about €50–70 per day with an apartment or private room and simple meals. A mid-range day with a 4-star hotel, two restaurant meals and one attraction costs about €110–160 per person, depending on whether the room is shared.

faq.question: Is Karlovac expensive?
faq.answer: No. Karlovac is cheaper than Zagreb for meals and drinks: an inexpensive meal is about €10 and a draft beer about €2.20. Hotel rates are moderate and stay steady across the year.

faq.question: How much does a hotel cost in Karlovac?
faq.answer: The main four-star hotels, such as Aminess Kadoor, Boutique Hotel Korana Srakovčić and Aminess Florian & Godler, usually start at about €90–120 per night for two. Apartments and private rooms often start around €50–60.

faq.question: How much do tickets to Aquatika and Dubovac Castle cost?
faq.answer: Aquatika costs €12 for adults, €7 for children 3–14 and €8 for students and pensioners. Dubovac Castle costs €3 for adults and €2 for children, students and retirees.

faq.question: How much is a beer or coffee in Karlovac?
faq.answer: A 0.5 L domestic draft beer costs about €2.20 in most cafés, and a cappuccino about €1.80. Tourist-oriented venues can charge more, up to around €6 for a beer.

faq.question: How far is Karlovac from Zagreb and how much is the trip?
faq.answer: Karlovac is about 55 km from Zagreb, roughly one hour by train or bus. Public transport is much cheaper than a private transfer, which can cost hundreds of euros per group.

faq.question: Is Karlovac worth visiting on a budget?
faq.answer: Yes. Accommodation, food and entry fees are below Zagreb and coastal levels, and many highlights, such as the star-shaped old town, riverside paths and Korana swimming spots, are free.

quickAnswer: Karlovac is one of the cheaper towns in central Croatia. Budget travelers can manage on about €50–70 per day, mid-range visitors on €110–160. Hotels usually cost €90–130 per night, an inexpensive meal about €10, a draft beer about €2.20, and the main sights (Aquatika €12, Dubovac Castle €3) are low-cost.
